newsitem.title: USA: P&G, Paragon diaper patent tiff continues.
newsitem.headline: P&G, Paragon diaper patent tiff continues.

text.p: Procter & Gamble Co lost a round in its pretrial skirmishes with rival Paragon Trade Brands Inc over competing diaper patent lawsuits.
The trial is scheduled to begin on February 3 in the U.S. District Court in Delaware.

Federal Judge Joseph Longobardi turned down a P&G request that he find Paragon's patent for a "low-bulk disposable diaper" invalid. In a decision, Longobardi said P&G failed to convince him that Paragon's patent for its core technology was either obvious or anticipated by other designs.
P&G sued Paragon in 1994 alleging Paragon products sold under store brand names infringe P&G patents used in the manufacture of "Pampers" and "Luvs".

"This ruling is inconsequential to the ultimate outcome of the trial that begins on February 3 when our patent infringement suits against Paragon will be heard by the court along with Paragon's counterclaims," P&G spokesman Mark Leaf told Reuters.
He added that the stakes in the case are very significant because disposable diapers, used by 94 percent of consumers, are a three-and-a-half billion dollar industry in the U.S.
A Paragon spokesmen was unavailable for comment.
